name: Swiftify ThreadScreen: Native SwiftUI thread/post detail view
notes:
ThreadScreen (src/screens/shared/ThreadScreen.tsx) is currently fully React Native using ScrollView + JS PostCard + ThreadTreeView/ThreadSummary/ThreadNavigator. Migrate to native SwiftUI for better scroll performance on deep reply trees.

Key requirements:
- Create a new native module (e.g., native-thread-view) following the NativeFeedList pattern
- Use SwiftUI List with lazy loading for thread replies
- Support nested reply tree rendering (parent → child → grandchild)
- Reuse FeedBridge serialization types (SerializedFeedViewPost, etc.)
- Bridge all interaction events back to JS (like, repost, reply, profile tap, etc.)
- Support thread navigation (jump to parent, jump to root)

This is the highest-impact Swiftification target after the home feed.

name: Integrate RichTextView into native PostCardView
notes:
RichTextView module (modules/rich-text-view/) is fully built with AT Protocol facet support (mentions, hashtags, links) and proper UTF-8 byte offset handling, but it's NOT used anywhere. Currently PostCardView (modules/native-feed-list/ios/PostCardView.swift) renders post text as plain Text() with no facet support.

Integration steps:
- Add RichTextView pod dependency to NativeFeedList.podspec
- Replace plain Text(post.post.record.text) in PostCardView with RichTextView
- Pass facets from SerializedRecord through the conversion layer
- Wire up onMentionTap, onHashtagTap, onLinkTap callbacks to the existing event dispatchers
- Note: RichTextView's tap handlers were removed from Text concatenation during build fixes and need to be re-implemented (possibly using attributed strings or a tappable text approach)

name: Integrate native embed views into PostCardView (images, video, links, quotes)
notes:
ExpoSwiftUIFeed module (modules/expo-swiftui-feed/) already has working SwiftUI embed components: ImageEmbed (1-4 image grid), VideoEmbed (with thumbnail), ExternalLinkEmbed (link cards), QuoteEmbed (quoted posts). These are only used in a test screen (FeedNativeTestScreen).

Integrate into PostCardView so the home feed renders embeds natively:
- Add ExpoSwiftUIFeed pod dependency to NativeFeedList.podspec
- Convert SerializedEmbed from FeedBridge types to ExpoSwiftUIFeed's PostEmbedData
- Add embed rendering below post text in PostCardView
- Handle embed interaction callbacks (image press, link press, quote press)
- This will make the home feed fully native-rendered (text + embeds + actions)

name: Swiftify NotificationsScreen: Native SwiftUI notifications list
notes:
NotificationsScreen (src/screens/notifications/NotificationsScreen.tsx) is currently React Native. It has a similar list-based structure to the feed and could reuse FeedBridge patterns.

Key requirements:
- Create a new native module (e.g., native-notifications-list)
- Create serialization types for AT Protocol notification objects (likes, reposts, follows, mentions, replies, quotes)
- Create a NotificationBridge module similar to FeedBridge for data serialization
- Design SwiftUI notification cell views for each notification type
- Support grouped notifications (e.g., '5 people liked your post')
- Bridge interaction events back to JS (tap notification → navigate to post/profile)

name: Swiftify Profile header and feed: Native SwiftUI profile view
notes:
Profile screens (src/screens/profile/MyProfileScreen.tsx, ProfileScreen.tsx) are currently React Native. The profile view has two natural Swift components:

- Profile header: Avatar, display name, handle, bio, follower/following counts, follow button — a natural SwiftUI component with smooth animations
- Profile feed: Can reuse NativeFeedList for the author's posts feed

Key requirements:
- Create a native profile header component with avatar loading, stats display
- Reuse NativeFeedList for the posts tab
- Support tab switching (Posts, Replies, Media, Likes) at the native level
- Handle follow/unfollow actions bridged back to JS
- Support pull-to-refresh on the profile feed

This is lower priority since profile views are less scroll-intensive than feeds/threads.
